content: If someone is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, the number to call is 1-844-764-7669. To prevent the spread of lice, wash all recently used clothing, hats, bedding, and towels in hot water or have them dry-cleaned. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not freeze it. This product is intended for single use only. Dispose of any unused lotion properly. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Discard this product appropriately when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. Possible side effects of this medication include eye redness or irritation, dry skin, or a stinging or burning sensation. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, do the same. Before using ivermectin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. The oral form of this medication passes into breast milk in small amounts, but it is unknown if this topical form does the same. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist.
